base_override.reason: Insurer payable-earnings base (Andrew, 2026-10-19; WORKER_SPEC step 4): ORI is a P&C/specialty insurer (EDGAR SIC 6351, Surety Insurance — within the rule's 6331/6351 scope) whose releases and annual report print operating income attributable to common shareholders (labelled net income excluding investment gains/losses, i.e. operating income) every period. Consolidated OCF capitalizes the reserve build and unearned-premium float (FY2025 OCF adjustments include +$354.9M of loss-reserve build and +$260.6M of unearned premiums and other policyholder liabilities), so the engine's OCF-based median base of $4.4470/share is not what common shareholders earn — the filer's own operating income was $3.15/share diluted in FY2025. Construction: ($935,900,000 + $845,100,000 + $749,500,000 + $797,000,000 + $792,500,000) = $4,120,000,000; / 5 = $824,000,000; / 251,313,860 diluted shares = $3.2788/share. Five-year average rather than 3-year median because an insurance cycle is longer than three years: the window spans the FY2021 investment-gain year, the FY2022-23 soft underwriting years and the FY2024-25 hard-market years. Figures are as printed in millions to one decimal place, so each carries up to $50K of rounding. With this base in force the one-notch tier_override softening (2026-10-15) is NOT applied — make_score refuses the pair as double-counting; the sector-misfit low confidence and alert suppression stay.
base_override.source: Net income excluding investment gains (losses) — the company's non-GAAP operating income attributable to shareholders — from the GAAP reconciliation table 'Overall Results Attributable to Shareholders' in Old Republic's 2025 Annual Report (the same reconciliation management presents in its earnings releases and 10-K reporting): FY2021 $935.9M, FY2022 $845.1M, FY2023 $749.5M, FY2024 $797.0M, FY2025 $792.5M (all as printed, in millions to one decimal). Cross-checks: the Q4/FY2024 earnings release (PRNewswire, Jan 23, 2025) prints FY2024 $797.0M and FY2023 $749.5M on the identical line; the FY2025 results summary prints FY2025 $792.5M, down 0.6% vs FY2024; the 2026 proxy pay-versus-performance table's Operating Income column prints the same five figures. Denominator: FY2025 diluted shares 251,313,860 (financials_history.csv shares_diluted, latest row).

capex_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine's sanity band anchors on the last FILED capex value under its candidate tags and Old Republic has never filed one in any period (last_filed_value is null in companyfacts), so no in-band estimate exists. The value is not unanchored — it is the filer's own FY2024 depreciation of $39,300,000, filed in its financial statements (see source), used as the maintenance-capex proxy under the 2026-10-18 depreciation-anchor clause because no capex was ever filed.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 (and every other year) under every candidate tag. The depreciation-anchor exception (Andrew, 2026-10-18) applies: for capex only, when no capex value was ever filed, a capex estimate may anchor on the filer's filed depreciation, within 0.1x–10x of that anchor; $39,300,000 is 1.0x the FY2024 filed depreciation anchor (and within 0.1x–10x of every filed FY2023–FY2025 depreciation figure). Maintenance capex for an insurer (premises, IT hardware/software, leasehold) is proxied by its own depreciation at the top of the filed range, the conservative end. The figure is immaterial to the verdict: $39.3M is about $0.16/share against the $3.28/share payable-earnings base actually scored, and that base is built from net operating income, which already carries the depreciation charge; the override's binding effect is to unblock the engine's OCF history.
capex_override.source: Anchor: the filer's own filed depreciation (us-gaap Depreciation, financials_history.csv da column) — FY2023 $33,000,000, FY2024 $39,300,000, FY2025 $35,400,000; the value used is the top of that filed FY2023–FY2025 range, FY2024's $39,300,000, as the maintenance-capex proxy. No capex value was ever filed: EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 74260 contains no PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment (or any candidate capex tag) fact in any period, and ORI's Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows present no purchases-of-property-and-equipment line — investing activities are maturities/sales/purchases of securities, other investments, and short-term investments, with premises/equipment spend folded into 'Other investments' / 'Other — net' and not isolable from the filing.

moat_against: Insurance capacity is close to a commodity — no network effects, low switching costs, brokers can move specialty business; pricing is set by the industry cycle, which is softening in several specialty lines

Combined ratio is drifting the wrong way — 92.6% (FY2023) to 93.9% (FY2024) to 94.7% (FY2025) to 95.3% in Q2 2026, with commercial-auto / long-haul trucking loss trends and a $40M reserve strengthening in Q2 2026
Title insurance is a housing-transaction derivative — premiums swing with mortgage rates and real-estate volumes, outside management's control
Operating income is flat in total dollars — $935.9M in FY2021 vs $792.5M in FY2025; all per-share growth has come from buybacks, not franchise growth, and H1 2026 operating income fell year over year

Reserve risk is the balance sheet — loss and LAE reserves are estimates; the favorable-development tailwind (2.4 points in FY2025) can reverse, as the slight unfavorable specialty development in Q2 2026 shows
moat_for: Diversified two-engine platform — Specialty Insurance (commercial auto, workers' comp, general liability, property, financial indemnity, warranty) plus the #3/#4 U.S. title insurer; title carried the result when specialty softened in Q2 2026 and vice versa in 2024

Conservative reserving culture over a century (founded 1923) — favorable prior-year loss reserve development in most recent years (2.4 points in FY2025, 2.9 points in Q4 2024) instead of reserve releases borrowed from the future
Sustained operating returns — operating ROE 14.1% in FY2025 and 12.1% annualized in H1 2026; combined ratio 92.6–94.7% across FY2023–FY2025, below 100% through the cycle

Capital-return engine — $1,708M returned in FY2024 and over $1B in FY2025 including special dividends; diluted shares down from 303.7M (FY2021) to 251.3M (FY2025); regular dividend paid for 44+ consecutive years of increases / 85 years of dividends
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat, 5/10 — the peer-consistent grade for a diversified specialty insurer (ACGL, AFG, AIZ and RNR all scored 5 in this sweep). Return evidence first, as required: fundamentals.json's roic_proxy series is null for every year and its gross_margin is null, because ORI files no OperatingIncomeLoss tag (annual operating_income is null in fundamentals.json) — for an insurer neither ROIC-on-operating-income nor gross margin is computable from the tags, so the return evidence is the filer's own operating ROE and combined ratio. Those support 5, not 7+: operating return on beginning equity was 14.1% in FY2025 (Q4 2025 earnings call) and 12.1% annualized in H1 2026 (Q2 2026 call), book value per share rose 22.0% in FY2025 inclusive of dividends to $24.21, and the consolidated combined ratio stayed below 100% through the cycle (92.6% FY2023, 93.9% FY2024, 94.7% FY2025) — returns above the cost of capital, earned by underwriting discipline and a diversified specialty + title platform rather than by any structural pricing power: capacity is fungible, brokers can move the business, and the combined ratio has drifted up for three straight years (95.3% in Q2 2026). A moat of 7+ would need durable pricing power or switching costs this record does not show. CAP = 2 + 1.3 x 5 = 8.5 years.
name: Old Republic International Corporation
one_liner: Diversified specialty P&C + title insurer with a moderate moat (5/10), scored on a five-year payable operating-income base of $3.28/share (not the float-inflated OCF base): at $39.68 the weighted IRR is 11.7% (Tier C, bear-to-bull band D to C) — it does not clear the 15% hurdle, which needs a price at or below the weighted IV@15% of $29.00.
